Postmortem of the database outage of January 31

2017-02-10

Last updated 2024-01-01 — share this post!

On January 31, 2017 GitLab.com experienced a prolonged database outage that lasted approximately 6 hours. An engineer intended to remove the replication lag on a secondary PostgreSQL database by deleting its data directory and re-replicating, but accidentally ran the rm on the primary.

The team realized the mistake within two minutes and halted the command, but approximately 300 GB of the primary's data had already been deleted. The remaining replication and backup mechanisms proved to be non-functional in exactly the configuration needed for fast recovery.

Root cause: no backup mechanism met the intended recovery point objective. Five of five planned recovery paths (pg_dump, LVM snapshot, Azure disk snapshot, replication, S3 upload) failed for independent reasons.

Impact: roughly 6 hours of downtime; approximately 5,000 projects and 5,000 comments lost; 700 new users signed up during the window could not be restored. We now run consistency checks on every backup mechanism at least once per week.

GitLab B.V.
